newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BLATTER ADMITS JAPAN TO HOST 2002 WORLD CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BLATTER ADMITS JAPAN TO HOST 2002 WORLD CUP FINAL.

text.p: Soccer's world governing body FIFA has admitted it plans to give the 2002 World Cup final to Japan while tournament co-hosts South Korea will stage the opening match and the third-place playoff.

"After this has got into the papers, despite an agreement to keep it secret, there is no point in denying it," FIFA general secretary Sepp Blatter said in an interview with Germany's Frankfurter Rundschau newspaper.
"But these are still just proposals for FIFA's executive committee to decide upon at a meeting in Barcelona on December 7."
The plans were agreed between Japan and South Korea at a meeting in Zurich last week. But until now FIFA has refused to confirm reports that a deal had been struck on the venue of the final.
"We agreed to keep quiet about what went on in the discussions and I have followed this," said Blatter, who also confirmed that FIFA's congress would also be held in South Korea.
"We had a very good and constructive discussion. We're on the right road."
South Korean and Japanese officials met for the first time in Zurich since the 2002 competition was awarded to both countries on May 31.
Relations between the co-hosts are often strained. Their rivalry is rooted in Tokyo's 35-year colonial occupation of Korea and the events of World War Two.
The next World Cup finals are to be held in France in 1998.
